correctness.rationale: For each cyclic zero gap, row parameter t runs from 0 to the gap length; sorting t descending then the next two gaps in reverse lexicographic order reproduces the full circular BWT and identifies exactly the three marked rows. Adjacency of those marked rows gives the complete 2/4/6 classification. The s-gap count is b_s=(1 if 3|s else 3) and a_s=(3s if 3|s else 3s-3); the marked-one double count transfers it to indexed words by a factor of n/3. Every quantifier, including periodic words, is treated explicitly. Independent direct rotation checks agree for 8,435 rooted gaps and 10,625 indexed words; the all-length proof does not depend on them.

originality.rationale: The known two-run structural theorem is excluded from novelty. The new content is the all-length four-/six-run distribution conditioned on exactly three binary ones, with a complete cyclic-gap adjacency criterion. The 2008 source only characterizes the single-block-per-symbol case; the inspected 2020 reversal and 2023 morphism results have different quantifiers and do not imply these exact indexed-word counts. No equivalent table surfaced from the checked published primary literature, published-finding corpus claims or accessible own records. Residual unindexed-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Run number of the circular BWT is a basic compression/indexing statistic. Counting its values conditional on three ones is a natural sparse-data problem: the full population is cubic in n, four-run strings are quadratic and six-run strings asymptotically dominate. The explicit cyclic gap criterion gives a complete infinite structural classification and exact all-length probability law, not a routine substitution or isolated small-instance table. A closed-form distinction between rare low-run and generic high-run members can guide sparse BWT test cases and combinatorial enumerations. The result does not claim a general BWT theorem for arbitrary weight.
